featured_reviews.review_text:
We approached Dr. Nitul Parikh with a lot of hopes after having a difficult history, and we are blessed with our baby boy in September 2025 – exactly as he had confidently told us after understanding our case in October 2024: “Next Diwali, you will celebrate with your baby.” His words gave us immense peace and confidence, and they came true.

For me, Dr. Nitul Parikh is like an image of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj – strict when it comes to following medical discipline and equally polite, caring, and nurturing with his patients.

He is like a elder brother to my wife, and I truly respect him and his entire “Vanar Sena” – the nurses, sisters, mavshi, and even the cleaners – who serve with dedication and warmth.

One thing that really stood out was that Dr. Nitul was always available on WhatsApp and calls during emergencies. This was something we lacked in our earlier experiences, and it made my wife feel even more secure and comfortable throughout her pregnancy journey.

We sincerely followed his guidance, and because of that, my wife had a smooth and swift delivery. Even if a family has no relatives around during pregnancy, Dr. Parikh’s own family (his wife and mother) makes sure to visit and support, creating a very homely and comforting environment. After our delivery, both his mother and wife blessed us with their kind words and presence, which was truly priceless.
We stayed in the deluxe room, which was very homely and well taken care of. At any hour, even midnight, the nurses and mavshi responded promptly with a smile, saying “Yes beta, kay zhala?” – such warmth is rare to find in hospitals.

For me, this hospital is not just a maternity and gynaec healthcare center – it is truly a temple, where every member of the team does their duty like a prayer. We are forever grateful to Dr. Nitul Parikh, Parikh family and his wonderful team for turning our hope into happiness. 🙏

featured_reviews.name: jovita pinto
featured_reviews.review_text:
I cannot thank Dr. Nitul and his entire team enough for the incredible support throughout my pregnancy and delivery journey. The maternity clinic and hospital are extremely well-lit, hygienic, and maintained impeccably at all times. I had a normal delivery, and what truly stood out was the team’s responsiveness—even in the middle of the night, they were prompt, calm, and supportive.

Overall, this was not just medical care, but a beautiful, well-managed, and compassionate experience. I would highly recommend Dr. Nitul and his team to any expecting parents looking for expertise, empathy, and exceptional care.

Your reproductive and women's health deserves expert attention at every stage of life. Whether you're dealing with irregular periods, PCOS, pregnancy care, menopause, or routine gynaecological check-ups, timely medical care can make all the difference.

Common reasons to visit a gynaecologist include:
• Irregular or painful periods

• Pregnancy planning and antenatal care
• Menopause-related concerns
• Preventive women's health check-ups

Early consultation helps identify concerns before they become serious and supports better long-term health outcomes.

Trying to conceive but not seeing the results you hoped for? IUI (Intrauterine Insemination) may be a suitable fertility treatment for couples facing certain infertility challenges.

You may benefit from IUI if you have:
• Unexplained infertility
• Mild male factor infertility
• Ovulation-related issues
• Cervical factor infertility
• Difficulty conceiving naturally after trying for several months

IUI is a simple, minimally invasive fertility procedure that places specially prepared sperm directly into the uterus to improve the chances of pregnancy.

Every fertility journey is unique. Read our full blog to understand how IUI works, who it is suitable for, and what to expect during treatment.

Irregular periods, pelvic pain, unusual discharge, or persistent menstrual discomfort should never be ignored. These symptoms may indicate an underlying gynecological condition that requires timely medical attention.

• Menopause management

Early diagnosis and the right treatment can help prevent complications and improve your overall reproductive health.

**Irregular Periods? It Could Be PCOD**

Irregular periods, unexplained weight gain, acne, or excessive hair growth may be signs of Polycystic Ovarian Disease (PCOD). Early diagnosis and the right treatment can help manage symptoms and improve your overall reproductive health.

Common signs of PCOD include:
• Irregular or missed periods
• Weight gain or difficulty losing weight
• Acne and oily skin
• Excess facial or body hair
• Difficulty conceiving

PCOD is a manageable condition with the right combination of medical care, lifestyle changes, and regular follow-up.

High-Risk Pregnancy? Expert Care Can Make All the Difference

A high-risk pregnancy requires specialized monitoring and timely medical support to help ensure the health of both mother and baby.

Some factors that may make a pregnancy high-risk include:
• High blood pressure during pregnancy
• Gestational diabetes
• Multiple pregnancy (twins or more)
• Maternal age above 35 years
• Previous pregnancy complications

Early diagnosis, regular prenatal check-ups, and expert obstetric care can help manage potential risks and support a safer pregnancy journey.

featured_reviews.name: Naseem Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Outside India currently and had my wife visit her clinic as she is currently pregnant. She had the most disturbing experience speaking with Dr. Vaishali Ghiya, the primary obstetrician at Carewel.

We had first visited Carewel 3 years ago for our first child. For the delivery, however, I had to take my wife to the hospital at 3 AM and there was no transport available. So we decided to go to the second hospital that we had registered in which was closer to where we live.

My wife had the Carewel file from her previous pregnancy which she carried  with her yesterday while visiting Carewel hospital. Dr Vaishali Ghiya was clearly upset that we chose to go to the second hospital on our list last time.

She made so many nasty comments that my wife almost cried. It's a shame that someone so educated has such a vile tongue. Some of the comments that she made are:

1. You guys are so poor. Maybe you cannot afford treatment here.
2. You should go to a government hospital
3. I will charge Rs 1500 to give an IV. Can you afford that? Should I start the treatment?
4. Why did you come here now? Why didn’t you go to the second hospital? Did something go wrong there?
5. Why are you coming when you are so far along?
6. There are two medicines, one for 1800, one for 2400 which one can you afford?

My wife and MIL, being kind and reserved, took these comments in silence. But is this any way for a doctor to talk to the patients? What kind of an example does it set for those working under her? Will nurses and wardboys also have the same attitude when a patient is admitted?

For perspective, my wife and I have a combined income of over 36LPA and, if we wanted, we could go to the most expensive hospital in Mumbai. We are shocked to see such an attitude from a doctor that treats women when they are at their most vulnerable. Honestly, I think we dodged a bullet here.

The irony is that my modestly dressed wife and I could pay for 12 deliveries at Carewel and still have money left over from our monthly income.

featured_reviews.name: Prasanna Mundinkeri
featured_reviews.review_text:
We started treatment with this doctor after 4 years of marriage. We underwent around 3 months of infertility treatment and after consistent follow-ups, we finally conceived. Unfortunately, at around 1.5 months we came to know that the baby was not growing, and we had to go through a very difficult loss. After taking a short break, we were blessed to conceive naturally.

During the next pregnancy, we faced multiple complications including gestational diabetes, low placenta placement, and bleeding in the 5th month. Throughout this challenging journey, the doctor was knowledgeable, supportive, and gave us confidence. Our due date was in January, but towards the end of pregnancy, due to diabetes-related concerns, we were advised for an early C-section and were blessed with our baby girl on 30th December 2023.

Again, we got good news in 2025. This pregnancy was comparatively smoother, but because of our previous pregnancy history and diabetes concerns, a similar situation was created again even before 35 weeks, and we were advised to prepare for an early delivery. Thankfully, we were blessed with our second baby girl.

Overall, the doctor is friendly, experienced, and knowledgeable, and we are grateful for the care that helped us become parents of two beautiful daughters.

However, one area where we felt improvement is needed is communication during critical decisions. In both pregnancies, the recommendation for C-section came in a very urgent and stressful manner, which left us feeling panicked and with very little time to fully understand, discuss, or mentally prepare for such a major decision. As patients, especially during emotional moments, clearer explanation and more time for discussion would have helped us feel more involved and reassured.

Still, we sincerely appreciate the doctor’s efforts and care throughout our journey and wish the team all the best.

A special thanks to the nursing and support staff, especially Aly, Hema, Sushma, and all the mavashies, for their care, kindness, and support during difficult and emotional moments. Their helpful nature, patience, and reassurance made a big difference throughout our journey and hospital stay. We truly appreciate their efforts and dedication.
